idea: Long-horizon (v2/v3, 6-12 month) async-events architecture for codexu / codex / crews / agent-comms. Builds FORWARD from D-002 (durable mailbox + channel wake) as foundation. 7 design axes: producer ecosystem, subscription transport, Scope A cross-tunnel, codex-as-crews-engine wire protocol, app-server idle-timeout interaction, heartbeat/presence convergence, replay/catch-up semantics.

candidateDirections.name: Evolutionary Layering (conservative)
candidateDirections.summary: Build v2 as incremental layers on D-002. Layer 1: D-002 ships. Layer 2: channel-wake for crews + bridge producers. Layer 3: app-server subscription RPC + idle-timeout. Layer 4: Scope A mailbox-on-server (demand-gated).

candidateDirections.name: Subscription-First Unification (ambitious)
candidateDirections.summary: Generic events/subscribe RPC at app-server level subsuming all notification patterns. Single model for all subscriptions with persistent cursor-based replay. High Rust-side investment + upstream conflict surface.

candidateDirections.name: Agent-Comms-Centric (demand-driven)
candidateDirections.summary: Focus v2 exclusively on agent-comms Scope B/C production quality; defer all producer ecosystem work until measurement shows actual demand. Exit-and-respawn remains default.

perAxisAssessments.axis1_producer_ecosystem: Hybrid per-producer-class: file-system events → app-server-native; git/timer → Node bridge-embedded; plugin events → plugin MCP server; inter-session → daemon control route.
perAxisAssessments.axis2_subscription_transport: Both-with-bridge: Node-side producers emit via MCP stdio bridge (session-scoped); codex-side via app-server WebSocket (connection-scoped); bridge = D-002 pattern (fs write + wake).
perAxisAssessments.axis3_scope_a_cross_tunnel: A3 (mailbox-on-server) is the architecturally-consistent path but DEFERRED — demand is speculative. Critical v1 decision: use logical addressing (sessionId) not physical (file paths).
perAxisAssessments.axis4_codex_as_crews_engine: Channels-leveraged hybrid: MCP bridge watches inbox/outbox JSONL, emits resource_updated, consumer pushes wake to MessageQueue2. File protocol remains authoritative. Channel wake is opt-in progressive enhancement.
perAxisAssessments.axis5_idle_timeout: Configurable idle-grace period (default 300s). D-002 doesn't create app-server subscribers (uses Node-side fs.watch). Pressure comes from Layer 3 (app-server subscription RPC), not D-002.
perAxisAssessments.axis6_heartbeat_presence: DO NOT converge — each layer keeps its own mechanism for different reasons. v2 adds a unified READ-ONLY presence aggregation query in daemon control server.
perAxisAssessments.axis7_replay_catchup: Two distinct patterns: cursor-based mailbox replay (messages, crews, agent-comms) vs state-snapshot synthetic events (subscriptions, fs changes). Intentionally not unified. D-002 inbox = Pattern 1 only.

v2BlockedOnV1: D-002 inbox envelope shape definition (blocks Scope A mailbox-on-server)
D-002 missed-wake recovery fixture (blocks app-server subscription replay)
D-002 happyMcpStdioBridge.ts producer pattern (blocks generic producers)
v1DecisionsThatBecomeIrreversible: Inbox envelope schema — must be versioned from day 1
Addressing model — must use sessionId (logical) not file paths (physical)
Wake signal URI scheme — must use stable agent-comms://inbox/<sessionId>
Consumer integration point — between-turns only; mid-turn is v3
Routing config shape — global-per-server-per-kind acceptable for v1; per-subscription is v2
questionsForOperator: Does N-001 (evolutionary layering) match your risk appetite, or do you want N-002 (subscription-first unification) for a more ambitious v2?
Is Scope A (cross-machine agent comms) actually needed in the 6-12 month horizon, or can it stay deferred indefinitely?
Should the codex-as-crews-engine task be filed immediately (material in Axis 4 is concrete enough), or wait for D-002 to ship first?
For Layer 2 prioritization: crews-channel-wake first, or git/timer producers first?
Is the 'exit-and-respawn stays default; in-session subscription is opt-in' framing correct, or should v2 flip the default?
